summary.text: A canal-sized schooner from 1867 lying roughly 10 miles off Algoma, Wisconsin, in deep Lake Michigan. Cold fresh water has left its deck-house and gear remarkably intact, but the depth puts it firmly in technical-diving territory.

summary.text: A large ocean-going freighter lost in a 1959 fog collision, now sitting upright and mostly intact in about 140 ft of Lake Huron within Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary, some 11 nautical miles north of Thunder Bay Island.

summary.text: A converted 1890 schooner-barge that foundered in a 1937 storm and now rests upright and in good condition roughly 4 miles off Point Betsie in Lake Michigan, at a depth reachable only by technical divers.

summary.text: A small wooden scow-schooner lost in an 1891 gale and found in 2018 near the Manitou Passage in Lake Michigan. Its masts still stand about 90 ft off the bottom in around 300 ft of water, a technical-diver wreck.

summary.text: A wooden schooner that grounded on a reef near Black River, Lake Huron, in 1870. Its hull lies in under 10 ft of clear water about 1.2 miles offshore, making it a favorite for divers, snorkelers and paddlers in Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary.

summary.text: A wooden steam barge driven ashore in a 1924 gale while sheltering off South Manitou Island. The wreckage, including its boiler, lies in 16 to 40 ft of water in the Manitou Passage Underwater Preserve.

summary.text: A wooden steamer lost in a snowstorm in 1885 off Dover's Point on North Manitou Island. The wreck sits in about 20 ft of water inside the Manitou Passage Underwater Preserve and is marked on dive charts.

summary.text: A steel freighter swamped and capsized in a 1913 Lake Huron storm, found by divers in 1976. It lies upside down and half buried in mud in roughly 175 ft of water northeast of Thunder Bay Island, inside the sanctuary.

summary.text: A steel freighter lost in the Straits of Mackinac in 1909 and rediscovered in 1980, lying from about 110 to 145 ft. Buoyed in season, it rewards advanced divers with anchors on the bow and an accessible engine room and holds.

summary.text: A three-masted schooner that sank in a snowstorm in 1886 off Long Island in Chequamegon Bay, Lake Superior. The hull is remarkably intact in about 24 ft, with its iron-ore cargo and deck fittings, and the site is buoyed each year.

summary.text: A wooden steamer lost in 1901 near Vermilion Point on Lake Superior. Ice and storms have broken it up, leaving mainly the boiler and scattered wreckage in 40 to 50 ft of water inside the Whitefish Point Underwater Preserve.

summary.text: An unidentified small sailing sloop from roughly 1880 to 1920, resting in about 25 ft of water just off Big Bay State Park on Madeline Island, Lake Superior. It is the only known vessel of its kind in Wisconsin waters and is protected by law.

summary.text: A steel freighter lost to a 1911 collision, now lying upside down in 125 to 150 ft off Whitefish Point in Lake Superior. Holds, engine room and steering quadrant can be reached by trained divers, in a preserve run as an underwater museum.

summary.text: A small packet steamer that grounded and burned off Michigan Island in the Apostle Islands in 1899. Hull remains and an artifact scatter, partly buried in sand, lie in shallow water over cobble and boulders; the site is on the National Register of Historic Places.
